solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disadvantage footballer's seen after 0-0 result?

indicators.note: seen after places the player's position behind the result in the answer

parts.note: a goalless match ends in a draw
a back is a defensive football player; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A football match ends goalless and a player is blamed for the downside.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a snag or handicap, a synonym for disadvantage.

clue.text: Cost is ridiculous, mounting up over time

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second
mounting up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: mad means absurd or ridiculous
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Prices are absurd and keep rising as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal makes DAM, written above AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'what's the damage?', the word is informal for the cost or bill.

clue.text: Attractiveness of short lane outside old city

indicators.note: outside says the trimmed lane goes around the city
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an alley is a narrow lane
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: The charm of a little lane on the edge of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it shortens 'lane' itself, but it trims the synonym; the ancient Sumerian city of Ur is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is charm or attractiveness that draws people in.

clue.text: Statesman's terrible racism revealed within covers of book

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: within says the rearranged letters go inside the outer letters
covers of means the outer letters of the word, like a book's front and back
terrible signals the letters are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: A politician's appalling racism is exposed between the covers of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes SMARCI from RACISM, inside B and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the Prussian statesman who unified Germany.

clue.text: Revolutionary female worker in the kitchen

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A radical woman is working in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, the chief worker in a kitchen.

clue.text: Telephone line into lady's private room?

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation goes inside the chamber word

parts.note: a bower is an old word for a lady's private chamber

explanation.surface: A phone line is run into a lady's private room.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOWER is British slang for the telephone, as in 'get on the blower'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is informal British slang for a telephone handset or phone line.

clue.text: Wait as one bound by fate having hesitation

indicators.note: bound by says the numeral is enclosed by the word for fate

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
I is the Roman numeral one
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone tied to destiny lingers, hesitant.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang around or linger, a sense of wait.

clue.text: First sign of winter and crossbred animals will make beastly noises

indicators.note: first sign of means the initial letter of the word

parts.note: a hinny is the offspring of a stallion and a female donkey

explanation.surface: With the onset of winter, hybrid animals start making noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse whinnies, making a gentle neighing animal sound.

clue.text: Record tigers being let loose on railway

indicators.note: being let loose suggests the letters run free and reshuffle

explanation.surface: Records note tigers escaping onto the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A registry is an official record or register of entries.

clue.text: Sickly stuff from Maureen and the girls

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the name Maureen
lasses are girls, especially in northern English and Scots use

explanation.surface: Something sickly sweet is served up by Maureen and her girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle-like syrup from sugar refining is cloyingly sweet, hence sickly stuff.

clue.text: Fish — four caught, still breathing

indicators.note: caught says the numeral is held inside the fish

parts.note: ling is a long cod-like sea fish
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four fish are caught and are still alive in the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still breathing is alive, which is what the adjective here means.

clue.text: Shameful bishop out of bed? In bed!

indicators.note: In says the bishop and the rising go inside the second bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A scandalous bishop is caught out of bed — or rather in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' appears twice: the first is part of 'out of bed' giving UP, the second is COT.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt means morally depraved or dishonest, hence shameful.

clue.text: Something rudimentary established by a new European

parts.note: a germ is the rudimentary beginning of something, as in the germ of an idea

explanation.surface: A newcomer from Europe establishes something basic.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Germany is a European, so the nationality is an example of the wider term.

clue.text: Senior women fussing no end, yes?

indicators.note: fussing suggests agitated rearrangement, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Older ladies fuss endlessly, nodding yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' looks like 'endlessly', but it is simply five letters of fodder alongside YES.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected senior woman in a field, so the plural means senior women.

clue.text: Getting rid of relations into the clutches of a psychologist

indicators.note: into the clutches of says the relatives are gripped inside the psychologist

parts.note: Carl Jung, the Swiss psychologist
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: Someone dumps their relatives on a psychoanalyst.
explanation.definitionFit: Junking means throwing away as rubbish, discarding.

clue.text: Get hold of a lot of sheets of paper — about a hundred

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go around the numeral

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of a batch of paper amounting to roughly a hundred sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain it, a direct synonym of get hold of.

clue.text: Time for a certain revolution? Yes, right!

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, as in voting

explanation.surface: Someone agrees enthusiastically that it is time for a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'certain revolution' is the Earth's orbit of the Sun, not a political uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelvemonth is the time Earth takes to complete one orbit of the Sun.

clue.text: Materials he removed from the discarded hats?

indicators.note: removed from says the two letters are taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: ex means former, cast off
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Fabrics he took out from a pile of cast-off hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he removed from the' leaves T; 'tile' is dated slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Textiles are woven fabrics, the materials used to make cloth.

clue.text: The first big character is one standing on two legs!

definitions.text: The first big character is one standing on two legs!

parts.words: The first big character is one standing on two legs!
parts.note: the capital A, first letter of the alphabet, is a three-sided figure resting on two splayed strokes

explanation.surface: A tall first-born giant is a biped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big character' is a capital letter, not a giant: capital A is shaped like this figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital A looks like a three-sided figure standing on two legs.

clue.text: Aggressive macho types given external check

indicators.note: given external says the check word goes around the outside

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
he-men are macho types

explanation.surface: Tough guys are frisked from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and intense, close to aggressive in manner.

clue.text: Jewish scribe of peculiar zeal, looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Jewish scribe is noted for his odd zeal in reviewing the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Ezra was a priest and scribe who brought the Law back to Jerusalem.

clue.text: Officer on board who may be using a rope?

definitions.meaning: the captain of a ship or boat

definitions.text: who may be using a rope?
definitions.meaning: one who skips with a skipping rope

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain is called this, and so, whimsically, is anyone jumping a rope.

clue.text: Prince's warning about British

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: about says the warning wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: an alert is a warning

explanation.surface: A prince issues a warning about Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort, so the name is a prince's.

clue.text: King has old wife attached to rope in ceremony of abasement

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a tow is a rope for pulling

explanation.surface: A king and his former wife are tied together in a humiliating ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowtowing is the Chinese ritual of kneeling and touching the head to the ground.

clue.text: Spooner's drunken group using mitts

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A drunk band performing with their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH BAND with its first sounds swapped gives BY HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitts is slang for hands, so doing something with them is doing it manually.

clue.text: After short time is making a protest at the back?

indicators.note: after says the protest word follows the abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
railing means complaining bitterly, as in railing against injustice

explanation.surface: After a brief while someone is complaining from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing means lagging behind others, so it is to be at the back.

clue.text: Loud old pop group associated with US city crime

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, a 1970s band
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A loud veteran band is linked with crime in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious crime, especially in US law.

clue.text: Northern bank open to view — characters within it twisted!

indicators.note: characters within it twisted says the inner letters swap order

parts.note: bare means exposed, open to view

explanation.surface: A bank in the north lies exposed with odd twisted letters inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner AR of BARE turns to RA. BRAE is a Scottish word for a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots and northern English word for a hillside or slope.

clue.text: Maybe a feller who keeps a diary?

definitions.meaning: a lumberjack, one who fells trees
someone who logs events in a record

explanation.definitionFit: A lumberjack cuts logs, and one who records entries in a log also fits.

clue.text: Generate new sort of drink

indicators.note: new sort of says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone creates a novel kind of beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea brewed from unoxidised leaves is a popular drink.

clue.text: Very English army officer in the Home Counties, slim and attractive

indicators.note: in says the three abbreviations sit inside the region's letters

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east, abbreviated SE
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An English army officer stationed near London is described as very slim and handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte describes someone gracefully slender and elegant.

clue.text: Given choice and was indebted

parts.note: choice as an adjective means the finest, the best
owed means was in debt

explanation.surface: A choice is offered and someone admits to being indebted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestowed means conferred as a gift, so it is a synonym of given.
